thread:
mia: Heads-up — after the keystore role change rolled at 03:10 UTC yesterday we started seeing a jump in mTLS handshake failures from APAC edge clusters. Proxy 502 spikes and backend shows: "handshake denied". Anyone else seeing this?

sam: saw Grafana alert earlier, was going to ping. Which service is getting the denies?

mia: proxy -> keystore decrypt calls failing. Short log sample: 
```
2026-03-17T03:42:11Z proxy-76fd: WARN handshake: client=svc-payments.apac.svc, err=TLSHandshakeDenied, detail=KV unwrap failed
2026-03-17T03:42:11Z keystore-2: ERROR kms: decrypt failed, err=AccessDenied: MissingRoleBinding
```

alex: AccessDenied on decrypt screams RBAC to KMS. Did the role change remove the proxy's service account from kms-decrypter?

mia: we changed the KeystoreRole to split ops/admin and svc roles; I thought proxy SA was included via GroupBinding. Might have missed one binding in APAC cluster.

priya: Can we confirm on KMS audit? If decrypt requests show 403 at KMS that's the root. KMS console: https://console.internal/kms/audit?filter=decrypt&time=3h

mia: tried that — the KMS audit index is empty for the proxy principal in APAC. Looks like decrypts never reached KMS (or audit sink filtered them).

ben: two ideas: 1) proxy might be hitting a fallback path that returns a soft deny before calling KMS, so no audit entry; 2) network path to KMS in APAC broken for that SA. Can you paste envoy/sidecar logs for the proxy?

mia: added an example of envoy log with auth header masked: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:42:11Z] envoy warning: upstream reset: upstream
[2026-03-17T03:42:11Z] keystore client: 403 AccessDenied for principal svc-proxy@apac -> KMS decrypt
```

ops-oncall: I can roll back the RBAC delta in 5m if you want. Rollback command: 
```
# revert rolebinding change
kubectl --context=apac-cluster -n infra delete rolebinding keystore-svc-binding-2026-03-16 || true
kubectl apply -f /manifests/keystore/keystore-svc-binding.yaml
```

alex: before rollback, collect forensic artifacts: full proxy pod logs, keystore pod logs, and the kube-audit events for RoleBinding changes (audit.k8s.io). Also capture cert fingerprint and SNI for failed connections.

ben: to get the cert fingerprint from the proxy logs quickly: 
```
kubectl -n apac logs proxy-76fd --since=10m | grep "peer_cert_sha256" | head -n 5
```

priya: open a short incident ticket and assign. security-bot: please create.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created: "APAC mTLS handshake failures after keystore RBAC change". Pager duty alert sent to oncall.

ops-oncall: rolling back now. Will patch binding and restart keystore pods if needed.

mia: rollback command applied, keystore pods restarted (kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore -n infra).

sam: monitoring ingress success rate now...

~10m later~

mia: Confirming: handshake error rate down from 3.8% -> 0.2% in APAC. Services recovered.

alex: good. Follow-ups: (1) fix the RoleBinding manifest so it includes the svc-proxy SA as explicit subject per-cluster, (2) add an automated test that simulates decrypt with a proxy SA during RBAC changes, (3) ensure KMS audit sink preserves decrypt events for service principals.

priya: Also we need better telemetry on the handshake path: SNI, cert fingerprint, upstream principal, and whether the decrypt reached KMS. Add structured fields in keystore logs: `kms_request_id`, `kms_response_code`, `keystore_cache_hit`.

ben: suggest a short-term alert rule: if mtls_handshake_denied_rate{region="apac"} > 0.5% for 3m -> paged alert. And a runbook step to check `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra keystore-*` and KMS audit for `Decrypt` entries.

mia: I'll open a PR: adds explicit SA subjects, adds unit test harness for keystore RBAC, and telemetry changes. Assigning tasks: mia -> PR and rollout plan, priya -> KMS audit sink config and retention, alex -> test harness and runbook update, ben -> alert + grafana panel.

security-bot: Reminders: attach the incident timeline to the PR, link audit logs to the runbook, and ensure customer-impact notes are filed if >5min outage.

mia: thanks everyone. We'll still do a postmortem if root cause involves policy drift; but glad rollback recovered traffic.

sam: nice triage. small note: add a gate in the RBAC deploy pipeline that runs a canary decrypt using the target SA before applying to all clusters.
